messages.subject: Trouble replicating a population abundance model of endangered macaws
parts:
Hi All,

I have been pointed here by the mathematics stack exchange user, JimB. In short, I am trying to get my head round the statistics that Monge et al (2009) used in this study (https://www.academia.edu/23659267/Censo_poblacional_durante_el_periodo_reproductivo_de_la_subpoblaci%C3%B3n_de_Ara_ambiguus_en_el_sureste_de_Nicaragua_y_norte_de_Costa_Rica_2009). I have attached the chapter from her thesis, which is the same but displays the equations correctly, in both English (for the text) and Spanish (for the images and formatting).

The original question can be seen in full here (https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/3185279/trouble-replicating-a-population-abundance-model-of-endangered-macaws)

And the equations in question here (https://i.stack.imgur.com/c353M.png)

But, essentially, I have no idea what they did or why. I'm pretty sure the choice of calculation makes no sense as it does not change much in proportion to area sampled or total size, but rather just greatly increase for each site added. Furthermore, I'm pretty sure they have made mistakes in their calculations too. There are definitely errors in their notation as A cannot = A/M, surely. I could be completely wrong though as I just cannot find where they got these equations from so that I can plug in my own data (and probably theirs again too) correctly. Can anyone help clear this up?

Thank you.

P.S. JimB also suggested that I use the pcount function in unmarked to analysis my own data, so although I am very novice at r, that is where I will start with my own analysis of the data.
